Rainfall-runoff events from rain and flow records

Source: R/events.R
find_events.Rd

Finds rainfall-runoff events in continuous records objectively, with the DMCA-based event separation routine (DMCA-ESR) of Giani et al. (2022). It needs no baseflow separation and one setting, rain_min, and applies at any time step that resolves the delay between rain and flow. Each event has a rain window and a flow window; a baseflow line joining the flow windows' ends gives each event's quick flow afterwards.

Usage

find_events(
  rain,
  flow,
  time = NULL,
  dt = 1,
  rain_min = NULL,
  max_response_h = 150,
  area_km2 = NULL,
  independent = TRUE,
  separation = 3,
  trough = 2/3
)

Arguments

rain

Rain per step (mm). Missing values count as zero.

flow

Flow per step, m3/s (or any units if area_km2 is not given).

time

Optional times of the steps, carried into the result.

dt

Time step, hours.

rain_min

Smallest rain intensity that counts at this time step, mm/h. By default 0.2 mm/h at an hourly step, scaled by dt^-0.5 (0.04 mm/h for daily data, 0.4 mm/h for 15-minute data), following the guidance of Giani et al. (2022) for British catchments. They found results insensitive between about 0.1 and 1 mm/h at hourly scale.

max_response_h

Passed to response_time_dmca().

area_km2

Optional catchment area, km2. With it, flow volumes are in mm and each event has a runoff ratio.

independent

Merge the events of one flood into one. At short time steps a long flood fed by several bursts of rain is cut into an event per burst, each a slice of the same hydrograph, so a list of the largest events counts one flood many times. With independent = TRUE, neighbouring events are one flood unless their peaks are independent by the rule used for UK peaks-over-threshold series: at least separation response times apart, with the flow between them falling below trough times the smaller peak; events whose flow windows overlap are always one flood. Merged events span all their parts, and their rain, peak and volumes are worked out afresh. This is the default. FALSE gives the published method's events unchanged, an event per burst of rain.

separation, trough

The independence rule: the least gap between peaks, in response times, and the share of the smaller peak the flow must fall below between them.

Value

A data frame with one row per event: event, the first and last rows of its rain window (rain_start, rain_end) and flow window (flow_start, flow_end), their times when time is given, rain_mm, peak_row and peak_flow (the largest flow in the flow window), and with area_km2, flow_mm and quickflow_mm (flow above the baseflow line) and runoff_ratio (quick flow over rain). Attributes: response (from response_time_dmca()), rain_min, dt and baseflow, the baseflow line.

Details

The routine, in brief:

  1. Estimate the response time with response_time_dmca(), and take the rain and flow fluctuations at its window. Rain fluctuations smaller than the largest that rain_min alone could cause are set to zero.

  2. An event's core is a run of steps where both fluctuations are non-zero; two steps where either is zero end it.

  3. Move the core's ends outwards to where the rain starts and stops (rain at or below rain_min delimits it), then to where the flow starts to rise and finishes receding (from the signs of the flow fluctuations, which are negative before the centre of mass and positive after it).

  4. Discard events with no dry spell around their rain, or whose flow window does not start before the flow's centre of mass and end after it; merge events that overlap.

This is an independent implementation from the published description and its reference code. One detail differs: overlapping events merge into one spanning all of them, where the reference code takes the end of the last. Rain windows that would run off either end of the record are discarded.

It was checked against the authors' reference code (https://github.com/giuliagiani/DMCA-ESR), run in Octave, on three synthetic records: two years of hourly data from a fast and a slow catchment, and ten years of daily data. The response times and all 663 event windows were identical. None of those records had overlapping events, so the one deliberate difference above was not exercised.

The work is done by the C core (pdm_find_events() and pdm_event_summary() in src/pdm_core.h), which other languages can call directly; options(pdmS7.engine = "r") runs the R reference implementation instead.

References

Giani, G., Tarasova, L., Woods, R. A. and Rico-Ramirez, M. A. (2022). An objective time-series-analysis method for rainfall-runoff event identification. Water Resources Research, 58, e2021WR031283. doi:10.1029/2021WR031283

See also

event_scores(), batch_events(), response_time_dmca()

Examples

river <- synthetic_catchment(years = 2, dt = 1, seed = 1)
events <- find_events(river$forcing$rain, river$observed, river$forcing$time, dt = 1,
                      area_km2 = river$truth$area_km2)
attr(events, "response")$response_h
#> [1] 6
head(events[, c("rain_start_time", "flow_end_time", "rain_mm", "runoff_ratio")])
